we developed an agent that learns to play in a simulated environment, using intrinsic motivation to learn a world model that can be used for object detection and localization.

we have created an agent with intrinsic curiosity that learns to predict its own behavior, and that this agent is able to learn a wide variety of behaviors in an unstructured environment without extrinsic reward signals.

we propose a novel architecture that allows an autonomous agent to self-supervise by generating novel structured behaviors, and we demonstrate its ability to generate a variety of complex behaviors, such as object attention, and improved object detection, localization and tracking performance.

we propose a novel approach to learning to play in an unstructured environment, which is a fundamental ability of human infants.
we are learning to play with intrinsic rewards in an environment with self-models.

a self-model can help an agent learn a world-model by generating novel and informative behaviors.
we can create agents that can learn to play in an unstructured environment by using intrinsic motivation and curiosity.
